label: Magazine
description: A premium visual magazine: research, flatplan, spreads, art, PDF.

prompts.voice:
YOU ARE WRITING FOR OUR MAGAZINE. Its promise: one thing, every connection. Each issue
takes one thing and follows it outward until the reader sees it is tied to everything.
The house style (house_style.md, above) is the brand: its voice, its recurring pages and
its rules outrank anything generic here.
Premium means *effortless to read and impossible to put down* - never dense, never
academic. A clever twelve-year-old and a bored expert must both finish the page.

ABSOLUTE RULES OF VOICE
- Tell a STORY. Never teach, never define, never explain "what X is" as a topic.
  Wrong: "Film photography is a process in which..."  Right: "In 1826 a man left a
  pewter plate in a window for eight hours and came back with a picture of his roof."
- Open on a person, a moment, an object or a number. Never on the subject's name.
- Concrete over abstract. Named people, real dates, real places, real quantities.
- Short sentences carry the weight. Vary length. No adverb pile-ups, and never
  "delve", "moreover", "in today's world", "it is important to note", "journey",
  "tapestry", "testament to", "at the end of the day".
- No bullet-point thinking dressed up as prose. No summary paragraph at the end.
- If a fact is uncertain, or you are not confident it is real, say so plainly in the
  text or leave it out. Never invent a citation, a quote, a date or a statistic.
prompts.pillars:
Research looks through these six lenses so the connection web has enough to stand on.
Not every issue needs all six on its pages — the web keeps the rings the research is rich in.
1. ORIGIN - how it came about, who had the idea, what problem or obsession drove them,
   the first breakthrough and what it actually looked like on the day.
2. EVOLUTION - what it became, the forks it took, what died, what survived.
3. TODAY - why it still matters, who uses it now and why, honestly.
4. STRANGE FACTS - did-you-know, the counter-intuitive, the numbers nobody expects.
5. THE UNDERLYING - the science, the mathematics, the philosophy, the psychology,
   and where real survey or study data exists, the data.
6. REAL WORK - actual practitioners, actual artefacts, actual output, shown and named.
prompts.research:
{{voice}}

SUBJECT: {{subject}}
{{angleLine}}
{{notes}}

{{pillars}}

Do the editorial research for one magazine issue on this subject. Go for the specific
and the surprising, not the encyclopaedic. Anything a reader could have guessed is
worthless here.

Research tools are available to you. Use them: facts you looked up beat facts you
remember, and every source you record has to be one you actually saw.

Return ONLY JSON:
{
  "title": "the issue's name - a cover line of 2 to 4 words that sells it from a newsstand. No colon, no subtitle: the thesis carries the explanation",
  "thesis": "one sentence, the idea the whole issue sits on. Never stated as a lesson.",
  "origin":    [{"fact":"...","who":"...","when":"...","why_it_matters":"...","source":"URL you actually opened, or empty"}],
  "evolution": [{"fact":"...","when":"...","why_it_matters":"...","source":"..."}],
  "today":     [{"fact":"...","why_it_matters":"...","source":"..."}],
  "strange":   [{"fact":"...","source_kind":"study|record|measurement|account","source":"..."}],
  "underlying":[{"field":"physics|maths|chemistry|philosophy|psychology|economics",
                 "idea":"...","the_number":"a real figure if one exists, else empty","source":"..."}],
  "real_work": [{"who":"...","what":"...","where_to_see_it":"...","source":"..."}],
  "uncertain": ["anything above you are not confident is accurate"]
}
6-10 entries per array. "uncertain" may be empty but must be honest.
prompts.plan:
{{voice}}

ISSUE: "{{title}}" - {{subject}}{{angleSuffix}}
THESIS: {{thesis}}
EXTENT: exactly {{extent}} pages.
{{notes}}

THE CONNECTION WEB - the issue's skeleton. Plan by walking it:
{{web}}

RESEARCH:
{{research}}

Build the flatplan.

STRUCTURE LAW (non-negotiable):
- Front matter: p1 cover, p2 statement, p3 imprint, p4-5 contents.
- Then sections. Each section OPENS WITH A PLATE: one full-page image on a RECTO
  (odd page number), no folio, no caption, one line of type that asks a question
  rather than naming a category. Section names never appear on any page.
- Because every plate is on a recto, EVERY SECTION HAS AN EVEN PAGE COUNT.
- The last page is the back cover.
- Density: D = design-heavy, M = mixed, C = content-heavy. Aim for roughly 30% D,
  40% M, 30% C, and NEVER more than two C pages in a row - that rhythm is what
  makes an issue readable rather than exhausting.
- Vary feature length as a real magazine does: 1pp, 2pp, and 4-14pp runs.
- WALK THE WEB. Sections are journeys through its rings, not one subject each. The first
  section's plate asks the web's question; the last section answers it with what the reader
  now holds and lands in their own life.
- Every page names its ring, and one or two LINKS to other pages it must bridge to -
  earlier or later - each with `why` and the `cue` word both pages share. Use the web's
  links; a page with nothing to bridge to is a page that does not belong.
- Every web thread is carried by at least three pages in different sections.
- THE RECURRING PAGES, in every issue: one `map` spread (two facing pages, an even page then
  an odd one) after the contents and before the second section - the whole web drawn; one
  `where-else` page or spread mid-issue; a `voices` page or spread ONLY if the research holds
  real people's own words with sources; and `in-your-hands` as the last page before the
  back cover.

Page types available: {{archetypes}}

Return ONLY JSON:
{
  "sections":[{"n":1,"label":"working label, never printed","question":"the plate line",
               "colour":"the section's colour world in words","from":7,"to":18}],
  "pages":[{"n":1,"title":"the page's own title","type":"one of the types above",
            "density":"D|M|C","section":0,
            "pillar":"origin|evolution|today|strange|underlying|real_work|none",
            "premise":"one sentence: what THIS page does that no other page does",
            "ring":"the web ring this page looks through",
            "links":[{"to":12,"why":"why these two pages belong together","cue":"the shared word"}],
            "threads":["names of web threads this page carries"]}]
}
Exactly {{extent}} page entries, n from 1 to {{extent}}, in order.
section 0 = front and back matter.
prompts.web:
{{voice}}

ISSUE SUBJECT: {{subject}}{{angleSuffix}}
THESIS: {{thesis}}
{{notes}}

RESEARCH (every claim carries the source it came from):
{{research}}

Draw the CONNECTION WEB for this issue. The magazine takes one thing and follows it
outward through every connection; the web is the issue's skeleton and every page will
stand on it.

- centre: the one thing, in two to five words.
- question: the question the issue opens on and answers on its last pages. A real question
  a curious twelve-year-old would ask, never a topic.
- rings: the lenses this research is RICH in, four to eight of: origin, evolution, science,
  culture, philosophy, psychology, people, places, art, where-else, future, you. Never pad
  a thin ring.
- nodes: the facts the issue stands on, twenty to forty, each in one ring, each with the
  source URL it came from in the research above. No node without a source.
- links: fifteen to thirty connections between nodes in DIFFERENT rings. `why` is one
  sentence a reader says "oh!" to. `cue` is a word or short name both ends share that a
  writer can put in the text: a person, a place, an object, a date.
- threads: three to five things that recur across the issue - a moment, a person, a place,
  an object - each with `cue` words that mark it in text, each able to appear in at least
  three different rings.
- wonder: the one image a reader will remember, in one sentence, with its `cue` words.
- accent: the colour most tied to the centre, as a name and a #rrggbb hex.
- motif: one visual motif taken from the centre itself (stitching for cloth, veins for a
  leaf, ripples for water) that a designer can draw as a rule or a divider.

Return ONLY JSON:
{"centre":"...","question":"...","rings":["..."],
 "nodes":[{"id":"n1","ring":"origin","fact":"...","source":"URL"}],
 "links":[{"from":"n1","to":"n7","why":"...","cue":"..."}],
 "threads":[{"name":"...","cue":["..."]}],
 "wonder":{"text":"...","cue":["..."]},
 "accent":{"name":"...","hex":"#rrggbb"},
 "motif":"..."}

intake.label: Subject
intake.question: What is this issue about? One subject, not a field — "film photography" rather than "photography".

intake.label: Angle
intake.question: What is the angle? Forty pages on a subject with no angle is an encyclopedia entry. What is the argument, the tension, or the question this issue is chasing?

intake.label: Extent
intake.question: How many pages? Leave it and the type's own default is used.

intake.label: Your own material
intake.question: Anything of your own to work from — corrections, sources, notes, files? Attach them or paste them; they outrank anything found by search.
